title: Compiler analysis report
preamble:
# Compiler analysis report

The compiler-analysis artifact emitted at build time. The compiler makes non-trivial choices during
lowering — series backing selection, capture-fact lifetime,
scope-activation completion paths, supersedure-key resolution, cooldown expansion, empty-cell
rejections — and these choices materially affect runtime cost,
behaviour, or correctness. The analysis report is the
author-facing surface for inspecting them.

This doc commits to **what the report contains** at the
language-spec layer. The format, delivery channel, and CLI
surface are runtime concerns, outside this document.

Paired with:
- [LSER.13.3] — series backing selection.
- [LCCO.5] —
  capture-fact lifetime.
- [LSCP.3] —
  scope-activation completion paths.
- [LRST.1.2] — supersedure-key
  resolution.
- [LCDB]
  — cooldown expansion.
- [RDSC] — natural
  home for the build-artifact format.

## What this is not

- Not a format spec. Format (JSON schema, structured-text
  layout, etc.) is a runtime concern.
- Not a delivery-channel spec. Whether the report ships as a
  build artifact, a log channel, or a CLI tool output is a
  runtime concern.
- Not a profiler. The report is build-time analysis, not
  runtime measurement. Runtime profiling lives in
  [NMET].
